transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 mins
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Tom (CISO - Parkside), Aisha (Head of Cloud), Dave (Eng Mgr), Sofia (Compliance)

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros, I'm Lena, AE for Redwood Inference. Marcus and Priya from our engineering team are here as well.
[00:12] Tom: Hey thanks, Tom Reynolds here, CISO at Parkside. We're looking at options for models + inference but the compliance piece is the blocker for us.
[00:21] Aisha: Hi, Aisha Malik, Head of Cloud. Key requirement is EU data residency for our EU customers and strict logging rules.
[00:30] Marcus: Great, thanks. To set expectations, we typically discuss three deployment modes: Hosted (region-specific), Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC or on-prem). Each has different guarantees around data residency and logging.
[00:44] Dave: Quick Q, when you say Hosted region, does that mean logs could leave the EU? We can't have transcripts stored outside EU for EU customers.
[00:52] Priya: Good question. Hosted can be region-scoped — for EU we can serve from an EU region. However, the difference is control: Hosted still has our control plane and standard logs; Dedicated gives you isolated capacity and stronger isolation; Private gives you full control over the control plane and where logs live.
[01:15] Sofia: From compliance: GDPR requires data of EU residents to stay in EU unless you have proper transfer mechanisms. Also, we're audited to FFIEC guidance and have PCI scope considerations for certain flows.
[01:29] Lena: Understood. For GDPR we usually provide region-specific hosting and can sign Data Processing Agreements. For Dedicated we can limit ingress/egress to region and for Private you can keep everything on-prem.
[01:41] Tom: What about logs? Our policy: no raw user-generated text outside the customer's region, and retention capped at 90 days for non-essential logs.
[01:51] Marcus: You can opt to disable retention of transcripts, or we can mask or redact PII at the edge. There's also an option for customer-managed KMS so encryption keys never leave your environment.
[02:06] Aisha: How does the KV cache and prefix caching work? We're worried that cached prompts might leak PII across requests.
[02:15] Priya: KV cache is ephemeral in-memory for latency; it's not persisted by default. For Dedicated/Private we can ensure caches are ephemeral per-instance and never serialized to disk. Also we have config to zero out caches after sessions.
[02:32] Dave: Is there any possibility that logs (like errors, traces) contain request bodies with PII?
[02:40] Marcus: By default, traces may include limited request metadata. We offer log scrubbing and can configure SRE level logs to exclude full request bodies. For Private deployments you control logging endpoints entirely.
[02:56] Lena: Also we support RBAC and SSO SAML for user access, and audit trails that meet common enterprise audit requirements.
[03:05] Sofia: Do you have SOC 2 and ISO attestation? HIPAA? We have a handful of clients that are health-adjacent and we'd like to know if there's HIPAA coverage or BAAs.
[03:16] Lena: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; for HIPAA we can discuss the scope — we have customers operating under HIPAA and can provide attestation and a BAA in specific cases. I'll send the security pack.
[03:27] Tom: What about key management? If keys are customer-managed, is there latency or integration complexity?
[03:34] Marcus: We integrate with customer-managed KMS in cloud (AWS KMS, Google KMS) and support HSM-backed keys. The latency is negligible for typical workloads; we fetch keys for startup and use envelope encryption. For on-prem Private we can integrate with customer HSMs.
[03:52] Aisha: Network connectivity: Do you support private peering/VPN into a Redwood VPC? We can't have traffic transit public internet for certain jobs.
[04:01] Priya: Yes: Dedicated and Private support VPC peering, private endpoints, and even air-gapped on-prem installs. For Dedicated we can do a private subnet and restrict egress; Private (on-prem) is fully behind your network.
[04:16] Dave: Timeline and pilot — we want to run a POC with ~500k tokens/day workload and compare latency/cost between Hosted EU variant and a Dedicated pool in EU.
[04:26] Lena: That sounds reasonable. Pilot could be Hosted EU initially for speed, then if you need isolation we can spin up Dedicated. We'll provide guidance on batching/quantization to optimize cost.
[04:38] Tom: One more: Do you keep copies of prompts/LLM responses for evals? Our policy is no long-term storage of responses for financial data.
[04:47] Marcus: We keep usage logs for billing and some aggregated metrics. For Hosted we retain minimal logs by default; you can opt out of storing transcripts or have them redacted. Dedicated can have retention policy set by contract and Private we don't store anything unless you enable it.
[05:01] Aisha: Is there a difference in SLA between Dedicated and Private?
[05:06] Lena: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; Private SLAs are negotiated since you're running in your environment.
[05:15] Sofia: Regarding audits, we need detailed audit logs showing who accessed keys, who deployed models, config changes. Is that available?
[05:25] Priya: Yes — we provide audit logs with admin actions, API keys usage, and model rollouts. For Dedicated we ship logs to a customer-managed logging endpoint (SIEM) if you prefer. For Private it's all in your logging stack.
[05:40] Dave: Any gotchas around model fallbacks and routing? We sometimes route to cheaper model variants and worry about differing data handling.
[05:48] Marcus: Good call — we can enforce routing policies that keep a request within the same residency constraints and ensure fallback models meet the same compliance profile. We'll surface model variant compatibilities in the catalog.
[06:02] Tom: For GDPR DSARs, do you offer data export and deletion APIs?
[06:09] Lena: Yes, we provide deletion endpoints and data export for customer data. For Hosted we process requests within agreed SLA; for Private you control storage so you process directly.
[06:20] Aisha: Are there any restrictions for PCI data? We can't have primary account numbers present in logs or be processed unless within PCI scope.
[06:28] Marcus: We recommend tokenization at the app layer before sending to inference for PANs. Also we can configure filters to redact PAN-like patterns server-side; however, if you cannot transmit PANs at all, Private/on-prem is the safest route.
[06:43] Lena: To recap the tradeoffs: Hosted is fastest to get started with region options but less control over logs; Dedicated gives you isolated capacity and better control over retention and network; Private gives you full control and is appropriate for the highest compliance needs.
[06:58] Sofia: Cost vs control — we'll need a clear TCO comparison. Our finance team will want to see reserved capacity pricing vs private deployment overhead.
[07:07] Lena: We'll put together a ballpark. For pilot pricing we can give you a one-month eval Dedicated estimate and Hosted costs plus a rough estimate for Private deployment engineering.
[07:17] Dave: Operationally, who manages model updates and rollouts? We can't have silent model changes that change outputs for customers under audit.
[07:25] Priya: We support pinned model versions and controlled rollouts (canary, A/B) and notify on model changes. For Dedicated you can pin a model version and schedule controlled updates.
[07:36] Tom: Any third-party subprocessors outside EU we should be aware of?
[07:42] Lena: We'll include subprocessors in the DPA. For Hosted EU we limit subprocessors to EU region. We'll share the list in the security pack.
[07:52] Aisha: Ok timeline: small pilot, technical deep dive, then security review.
[07:58] Lena: Perfect. We'll send docs and set up the deep dive.
[08:02] Sofia: A couple of minutia — do you provide data residency guarantees in contract?
[08:08] Marcus: Yes for Dedicated and Private we can contractually commit to residency and provide audit evidence. Hosted region is typically stated in the agreement with the usual DPA clauses.
[08:19] Dave: For the pilot we'll need an API key model that supports IP restrictions and short-lived tokens.
[08:26] Priya: Supported — we have scoped API keys, IP allowlists, and short-lived tokens via STS.
[08:34] Tom: Anything else on encryption in transit and at rest?
[08:38] Marcus: TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest by default; customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM supported.
[08:45] Lena: Great, I'll follow up with the security pack and pricing. Marcus will share the VPC and KMS docs. Can we target the technical deep dive for next Tuesday?
[08:56] Aisha: Next Tue works for the infra folks.
[09:00] Sofia: We'll provide our retention policy and data redaction rules ahead of that.
[09:06] Lena: Thanks everyone, we'll recap via email and share the items.
[09:10] Tom: Thanks all.

Notes: occasional transcription errors observed (Redwood "dedicate" vs "dedicated", "K-V cache" vs KV cache).

End of transcript.
